name: Frontend Interface
description: Gives a separate frontend, such as a web or mobile app, everything the terminal has about a session as plain data: the events and controls as JSON, and one picture of the run with its steps, helpers and their solutions, cost, files changed, messages sent and whether each was taken up, the open question and how it ended.
purpose: Let any frontend that is not a terminal draw and steer an AI session from plain data, without knowing the harness or the terminal.
approach: Carry each event and control as the data form the contract defines, fold them into one picture of the run, and keep everything specific to a terminal out of it.
out_of_scope: How a screen looks, the transport (a socket, a stream, polling), a consumer's data model and settings, drawing as text (Terminal Experience), and choosing which structure to show (Structure In View, whose result it carries).
milestones: 1. Every event and control kind crosses to plain data and back, the run facts a frontend needs are in the picture, and nothing specific to a terminal leaks (authoritative metric metric-frontend-interface).
knowledge: Placement against siblings: the contract and its adapters stay in AI Session Experience; this child is what a remote UI consumes, so it owns the plain-data form of the run (cost, helpers, changed files, steer acknowledgement, pending input), which the terminal child holds only as text. Extend before adding: it could have been a metric stage of Terminal Experience, but a frontend has different alternatives (a snapshot, a delta stream) and fails differently (a leaked escape code, a lost steer acknowledgement), so it has its own metric and arms.
measures_of_success: Share of scripted cases right: each event and control kind round-trips to a plain JSON form, each run fact is present, and no terminal-specific text appears.
inputs: Events (objects or dicts), controls, optionally a Structure In View result.
outputs: A JSON-ready picture of the run; the dict of one event or control and the object back.
effects: None: pure functions over what they are given.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("frontend-interface", {"events": [...], "controls": []})` returns the picture. A backend maps its own stream to the contract's events and sends the picture, or each event, to the page.
